newsitem.title: USA: Pheonix of U.S. wins 2.7 mln bbl Iraq oil contract.
newsitem.headline: Pheonix of U.S. wins 2.7 mln bbl Iraq oil contract.

text.p: A small Virginia-based energy company has signed a contract with Iraqi State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) to buy 2.7 million barrels of Basrah Light crude oil, a company official confirmed on Friday.
The contract, which is still awaiting United Nations approval, was won by the privately-held Pheonix International under the second phase of the "oil-for-food" program launched in June.

The Pheonix contract would run through December, translating into a daily rate of around 25,000 barrels per day (bpd), a relatively large contract for the obscure, McLean, Va., firm headed by Samir Vincent.
The other U.S. companies which are slated to lift Iraqi oil are Chevron Corp, Coastal Corp, Mobil Corp and privately held trader Bayoil.
Texaco Inc sources said this week that the company would not seek to renew the 10,000 bpd contract it held in the first round following unsuccessful talks with SOMO.

The oil-for-food deal was implemented as an exception to broad U.N. sanctions imposed in 1990 after the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait. The program allows Iraq to sell $2.14 billion worth of crude from June to December in two separate 90-day periods of $1.07 billion each.

Iraq's oil minister, Amir Muhammed Rasheed, said earlier this year that oil companies from countries which had supported an easing in sanctions would be favored with oil business. Russian companies were the biggest gainers, while British and Japanese companies have so far been cut out of the second phase.

But among U.S. companies all but Texaco have had their contracts renewed, even though the U.S. government has been by far the most stalwart in its opposition to any easing in the strict control on Iraq's imports and exports.
